cases.title: CLR WORK inside Bond resets SDT to its default date
cases.notes: Defaults table, pp. 50-51. CLR WORK is scoped to the worksheet you are standing in, so it must be pressed inside Bond.

cases.title: CPN default is zero after CLR WORK
cases.notes: Default value 0 from the p. 51 defaults table. Display string assumes the default DEC=2 format; the guidebook prints the default as bare '0'.

cases.title: RDT default matches SDT default
cases.notes: p. 51 defaults table. RDT equalling SDT on a fresh worksheet is precisely what makes the p. 50 Error 6 note fire.

cases.title: RV default is 100 percent of par
cases.notes: p. 51 defaults table. The worked example on p. 53 confirms the 100.00 display string when RV is left untouched.

cases.title: Day-count toggle defaults to ACT
cases.notes: p. 50 defaults table lists ACT/360 default = ACT. This position is a toggle, not a numeric field.

cases.title: Coupon frequency toggle defaults to 2/Y
cases.notes: p. 51 defaults table lists '2/Y, 1/Y' default = 2/Y. Confirmed by the worked example, which leaves this position alone and displays 2/Y (p. 53).

cases.title: Navigating a freshly-reset worksheet raises Error 6
cases.notes: p. 50 states that navigating with the arrow keys before entering values raises Error 6, clearable with CE/C. Root cause per p. 85: a calculation was attempted with RDT earlier than or the same as SDT, and both default to 12-31-1990. The exact arrow count at which it fires is NOT specified by the guidebook - p. 50 only says navigation triggers it. This case assumes it fires when a computed position (YLD/PRI/AI) is reached; treat the key count as approximate.

cases.title: Opening the worksheet displays the current SDT
cases.notes: Worked example row 1, p. 53: '2nd BOND -> SDT = 12-31-1990'. Distinct from bond-defaults-clr-work-sdt: the example does NOT press CLR WORK, so this asserts that opening the worksheet shows the CURRENT SDT (p. 52), which here happens to still be the 12-31-1990 default. This row is what establishes the at-defaults precondition for the rest of the example.

cases.title: Settlement date entered as mm.ddyy displays in US date format
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. NOTE the guidebook prose says the bond settles June 12, 2004, but the printed keystrokes and the printed display both say 2006. Worked example wins. Two-digit year 06 -> 2006 within the 1980-2079 window (p. 51); the pivot rule itself is never stated.

cases.title: Coupon rate entered as a percentage of par
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. CPN is the annual rate as a percent of par (p. 51), not the dollar coupon.

cases.title: Redemption date entered as mm.ddyy displays in US date format
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. Prose says maturity December 31, 2005; keystrokes and display say 2007. Worked example wins.

cases.title: Redemption value left at its default for a to-maturity analysis
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. Redeemable at 100% of par, so RV keeps its default. Displayed without the entry annotation because nothing was keyed in.

cases.title: 2ND SET flips the day-count toggle from ACT to 30/360
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. Single 2ND SET press flips ACT -> 360. Precondition: toggle sits at its ACT default.

cases.title: Coupon frequency left at two coupons per year
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. Semiannual bond, so the 2/Y default stands (M = 2 in the appendix formulas).

cases.title: Yield to maturity entered as a percentage
cases.notes: Worked example, p. 53. YLD is the annual nominal yield in percent; Y = YLD / 100 = 0.08 in the appendix formulas (p. 77).

cases.title: Compute bond price from yield, 30/360, semiannual, more than one coupon remaining
cases.notes: PRIMARY GOLDEN CASE. Worked example, pp. 53-54. Quoted per $100 of par. Exact value 98.56275, truncating/rounding to 98.56 at DEC=2. Verified against the appendix multi-period price formula (p. 78) with N=4, A/E=0.9, DSC/E=0.1, R=0.07, M=2, Y=0.08: 13.16110 + 88.55165 - 3.15000 = 98.56275. The printed bond formulas agree with this example - no sign-convention defect here, unlike the TVM PMT formula. Precondition: worksheet at defaults before the sequence (the example's first display shows SDT = 12-31-1990). No sign convention applies; PRI is a positive magnitude.

cases.title: Accrued interest is auto-computed and requires no CPT
cases.notes: PRIMARY GOLDEN CASE. Worked example, p. 54. Quoted per $100 of par. AI = PAR x R/M x A/E = 100 x 0.035 x 0.9 = 3.15 exactly (p. 78), so no rounding caveat. Reached with a single arrow press - AI is auto-compute, never CPT.
